Mechanism reasoning, asset construction, and evidence attribution operate within one agentic loop. abstract: Generating interactive 3D assets from a single image requires realistic appearance, fidelity to the depicted object, and plausible physical behavior. Yet detailed geometry alone does not determine how an object should move or deform. We introduce PhysAg3D, which couples 3D generative models with agentic reasoning and tool use. A vision-language agent first infers semantic parts, candidate interactions, and physical priors from the image; a 3D generator then produces a textured whole-object mesh from the same image. A hierarchical interaction representation links these revisable priors to mechanisms and the generated surfaces they control, organizing interaction construction and refinement. Guided by this representation and observations of the mesh, the agent uses geometric and physical tools to construct parts, joints, deformable regions, and surface bindings while retaining useful generated geometry and materials. Rendered interactions and execution measurements guide targeted revisions within a fixed budget. The framework accommodates both rigid articulation and compliant deformation. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations on real photographs and external benchmarks demonstrate detailed, image-aligned assets with plausible interactions. Ablations support bounded refinement and source-surface preservation. Project Page: supra-3d.github.io/PhysAg3D.

sections.body: A single image leaves hidden mechanisms and physical parameters undetermined, and a generated mesh may not expose the parts needed for interaction. In PhysAg3D, a vision-language agent infers semantic parts, candidate interactions, and physical priors from the image, while a 3D generator produces a textured whole-object mesh from the same image. A hierarchical interaction representation links these priors to mechanisms and to the visible surfaces they control. The section states that both rigid articulation and compliant deformation are supported. Figure 1 shows development examples of a camera, a laptop stand, and headphones with compliant ear pads, two of them with recorded simulated states.
sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.headline: PhysAg3D pairs a 3D generator with a vision-language agent that builds revisable interaction mechanisms on the generated mesh.

sections.body: Image-to-3D generators, including TRELLIS and UniLat3D, supply detailed geometry and materials. Articulation work such as PartNet-Mobility, Particulate, and Instruct-Particulate predicts parts, joints, and motion from shapes or images. Agentic systems such as Articulate-Anything, ArtiCraft, and aDSL build or revise articulated models through programs, tests, or structured feedback. The section positions PhysAg3D as connecting intended interactions, physical entities, exported bindings, and observed surface responses, including compliant regions whose simulation and visible geometry differ.
sections.heading: 2 Related Work
sections.headline: Related work spans image-to-3D generation, articulation prediction, agentic asset modeling, and simulation substrates.

sections.body:
Each candidate is represented by interaction intent $S$, physical structure $K$, and concrete realization $X$, linked by correspondences that map entities to visible regions of the generated mesh. Rigid vertices follow their assigned body transform. For a compliant region, visible vertices follow physical nodes through a weight matrix, written as:

$$
V_{t}=V_{rest}+W(P_{t}-P_{rest})
$$

Refinement uses renders, source-surface checks, and MuJoCo execution, with at most two Builder repairs after the initial construction. Unmet requirements and unresolved discrepancies stay recorded, and a preview can be returned without a valid dynamic trajectory.
sections.heading: 3 Method
sections.headline: The method links an image-derived interaction hierarchy to construction and bounded refinement, with rigid and compliant bindings to visible surfaces.

sections.body: Evaluations cover 50 in-the-wild objects with 110 actions, PhysXVerse, PhysX-Mobility, PhysX-Bench, and 102 valid human evaluations. On the in-the-wild set, PhysAg3D reports ACR of 91.3% and FVSP of 88.0%, against 66.8% and 42.0% for the best baseline on each. On PhysXVerse, PSNR is 24.26, which the text reports as 2.74 dB above the strongest baseline. In the human study, mean input-consistency is 4.63 versus 2.98 for the next method. Full pipeline improves KPS and MPS over One-shot by 19.68 and 17.26 points, and removing surface preservation lowers RQS by 17.68. The authors state that playback and human judgments do not establish calibrated dynamics or contact stability.
sections.heading: 4 Experiments
sections.headline: PhysAg3D leads most reported metrics across four evaluations, and ablations support bounded refinement and surface preservation.

sections.body: The conclusion summarizes PhysAg3D as a method for generating interactive 3D assets from a single image. The hierarchical representation connects interaction requirements, physical mechanisms, and visible surfaces to guide construction and feedback-based refinement. The authors state that experiments support appearance preservation and plausible interactions, and that ablations indicate benefits from refinement and surface preservation. They identify recovering hidden structure and material properties as a remaining limitation. The section also contains the funding acknowledgment.
sections.heading: 5 Conclusion
sections.headline: The conclusion restates the hierarchical representation and names recovering hidden structure and material properties as a remaining limitation.

sections.body: The appendix defines the interaction levels S, K, and X, the correspondence and source maps, and the binding checks for rigid and compliant regions. Table 6 lists the runtime configuration: three Builder attempts in total, at most two host physical validations, and at most one structural replan. It gives the motion-range reduction sequence, acceptance tolerances in units of the asset diagonal D, and deformation criteria for compliant regions. It also specifies the output-selection order, metric definitions for the in-the-wild evaluation, baseline scoring notes, and the ablation configuration.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix lists representation details, binding checks, runtime budgets, motion-range and deformation criteria, output selection, and evaluation definitions.
